content.text:
Silhouette: Horizontal red fox frame carried on two hind legs, barn owl wings in place of the forelegs. Host frame: the red fox sets the outline, body size, and overall frame. It is a single creature combining a red fox and a barn owl. The head is that of the red fox, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: the body and legs are those of the red fox, with its own dense fur on the face, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs, and tail; the coat is plain, with no stripes or spots. From the barn owl, as parts and materials on the red fox's own body: broad wings of layered flight feathers in place of the forelegs, standing on two hind legs, with wings sized for flight; layered contour feathers in its own colors grown from the skin as the red fox's own covering over the shoulders and neck, replacing the red fox's dense fur there and conforming to the red fox's body, sized to the red fox's body and following its contours. Every covered part keeps the red fox's own length and shape; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, while the face, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs, and tail keep the red fox's own dense fur; deep keel and heavy flight chest. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical, with recognizable limbs and visible sense organs. Habitat cue (desert): larger ears and longer tail for shedding heat. Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws, and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid creature silhouette**
I'm planning a single creature that uses a red fox outline and body, with barn owl wings replacing the forelegs, and a clear fox head with visible eyes and plain dense fur.
**Drafting natural history illustration**
I'm composing a side three-quarter, full-body illustration of the red fox with barn owl wings replacing the forelegs, feathered shoulders and neck, larger ears, longer tail, and natural lighting on a plain light background.
**Refining winged anatomy**
I'm planning a regeneration that replaces the forelegs entirely with full wings, so the creature has wings as arms and no separate forelegs.
